(a) after verbs of motion or of speaking and other words with the idea of direction: ἔρχομαι, ἀναβαίνω, πορεύομαι, λέγω, ἐπιστολή, etc., Mt 3:14, Mk 6:51, Lk 11:5, Jo 2:3, Ac 9:2, al. mult.; metaph., of mental direction, hostile or otherwise, Lk 23:12, Jo 6:52, II Co 7:4, Eph 6:12, Col 3:13, al.; of the issue or end, Lk 14:32, Jo 11:4, al.; of purpose, Mt 26:12, Ro 3:26, I Co 6:5, al.; πρὸς τό, c. inf., denoting purpose (cf. M, Pr., 218, 220; Lft., Notes, 131), Mt 5:28, Mk 13:22, Eph 6:11, I Th 2:9, al.;
(b) of close proximity, at, by, with: Mt 3:10, Mk 11:4, Lk 4:11, Ac 3:2, al.; after εἶναι, Mt 13:56, Mk 6:3, Jo 1:1, al.
2. Of time,
(a) towards (Plat., Xen., LXX: Ge 8:11, al.): Lk 24:29;
(b) for: πρὸς καιρόν, Lk 8:13, I Co 7:5; πρὸς ὥραν, Jo 5:35, al.; πρὸς ὀλίγον, Ja 4:14.
3. Of relation
(a) toward, with: Ro 5:1, II Co 1:12, Col 4:5, I Th 4:12, al.;
(b) with regard to: Mt 19:8, Mk 12:12, Ro 8:31, al.;
(c) pertaining to, to: Mt 27:4, Jo 21:22, Ro 15:17, He 2:17 5:1;
(d) according to: Lk 12:47, II Co 5:10, Ga 2:14, Eph 3:4 4:14;
(e) in comparison with: Ro 8:18.
IV. In composition: towards (προσέρχομαι), to (προσάγω), against (προσκόπτω), besides (προσδαπανάω).

title: προσάββατον
content:
† προ-σάββατον, -ου, τό, [in LXX: Ps 91 (92) tit., א (שַׁבָּת) Ps 92 (93) tit., Jth 8:6*;]

the day before the Sabbath: Mk 15:42 (L, Tr., txt., πρὸς σ.).†

title: προσαγορεύω
content:
προσ-αγορεύω, [in LXX: De 23:6 (7) (דָּרַשׁ), II Es 10:11, B:1 (ידה hith.), Wi 14:22, I Mac 14:40, II Mac 1:36 4:7 10:9 14:37*;]

to address, greet, salute; hence, to call by name, address, style: c. dupl. acc., pass., He 5:10.†

title: προσάγω
content:
προσ-άγω, [in LXX chiefly for קרב hi., also for נגשׁ etc.;]

1. trans., to bring or lead: c. acc. et dat., Ac 16:20; metaph., τ. θεῷ, I Pe 3:18; seq. ὧδε, Lk 9:41; pass., c. dat., Mt 18:24 (προσηνέχθη, T); in forensic sense, to summon: Ac 12:6 (προαγαγεῖν, T, WH, mg., R).
2. Intrans., to draw near, approach (Jos 3:9, Je 26 (46):3, al.): c. dat., Ac 27:27 (WH, προσαχεῖν).†

title: προσαγωγή
content:
* προσ-αγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ, (< προσάγω),

1. a bringing to.
2. approach, access (v. Lft., Notes, 284; MM, xxi): Ro 5:2, Eph 2:18 3:12 (but v. Ellic., Eph., 59 f., where the transitive sense "introduction" is advocated).†

title: προσαιτέω
content:
προσ-αιτέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Jb 27:14*;]

1. to ask besides.
2. to continue asking; hence, to importune, beg, ask alms: Jo 9:8.†

title: προσαίτης
content:
*† προσαίτης, -ου, ὁ,

a beggar: Mk 10:46, Jo 9:8.†

title: προσαναβαίνω
content:
προσ-ανα-βαίνω, [in LXX: Ex 19:23, al. (עלה);]

1. to go up besides.
2. to go up higher: Lk 14:10.†

title: προσαναλίσκω
content:
* προσ-αναλίσκω,

to spend besides: Lk 8:43 (WH, R, mg., om.).†

title: προσαναπληρόω
content:
** προσ-αναπληρόω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Wi 19:4*;]

to fill up by adding to, to supply fully: II Co 9:12 11:9.†

title: προσανατίθημι
content:
* προσ-ανα-τίθημι,

to lay on or offer besides; mid.,
(a) to lay on oneself in addition, undertake besides;
(b) c. gen. pers., of giving or obtaining information, to consult, communicate: Ga 1:16 2:6 (Lft., in l.; cf. ἀνα-τίθημι).

title: προσανέχω
content:
* προσ-αν-έχω,

to approach: v.l. for προσαχέω, Ac 27:27 L.+

title: προσαπειλέω
content:
** προσ-απειλέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Si 13:3 א*;]

to threaten further: Ac 4:21.†

title: προσαχέω
content:
*† προσ-αχέω, -ῶ, Doric for προσηχέω,

to resound: of land perceived by the roar of the surf, Ac 27:27 (WH, mg., cf. προσάγω).†

title: προσδαπανάω
content:
*† προσ-δαπανάω, -ῶ,

to spend besides: c. acc., Lk 10:35.†
SYN.: προσαναλίσκω.

title: προσδέομαι
content:
προσ-δέομαι, [in LXX: Pr 12:9 חָסֵר, Si6*;]

to want further, need in addition: Ac 17:25.†

title: προσδέχομαι
content:
προσ-δέχομαι, [in LXX chiefly for רצה;]

1. to receive to oneself, receive favourably, admit, accept: c. acc. pers., Lk 15:2, Ro 16:2, Phl 2:29; c. acc. rei, Ac 24:15 (R, mg.), He 10:34 11:35.
2. to expect, look for, wait for: c. acc. pers., Lk 12:36; c. acc. rei, Mk 15:43, Lk 2:25, 38 23:51, Ac 23:21, Tit 2:13, Ju 21 (cf. δέχομαι).†

title: προσδοκάω
content:
προσ-δοκάω, -ῶ (the simple verb exists only in the forms δοκέω, -εύω), [in LXX: Ps 103 (104):27 (שׂבר pi.), etc.;]

to await, expect: Mt 24:50, Lk 3:15 12:46, Ac 27:33 28:6; c. acc. pers., Mt 11:3, Lk 1:21 7:19, 20 8:40, Ac 10:24; c. acc. rei, II Pe 3:12–14; c. acc. et inf., Ac 28:6; c. inf., Ac 3:5.†

title: προσδοκία
content:
προσδοκία, -ας, ἡ (< προσδοκάω), [in LXX: Ge 49:10 (יִקְהָה), Ps 118 (119):116 (שֵׂבֶר), Wi 17:13, Si 40:2, al.;]

expectation: c. gen. obj., Lk 21:26; c. gen. subjc., Ac 12:11.†

title: προσεάω
content:
*† προσ-εάω, -ῶ,

to permit further: Ac 27:7.†

title: προσεγγίζω
content:
† προσ-εγγίζω, [in LXX chiefly for נגשׁ, קרב;]

1. trans., to bring near (Luc.).
2. Intrans., to approach: c. dat., Mk 2:4 (WH, προσενέγκαι).†

title: προσεδρεύω
content:
** προσεδρεύω (< πρόσεδρος, sitting near), [in LXX: I Mac 11:40*;]

1. to sit near.
2. to attend regularly: c. dat., I Co 9:13, Rec. (v.s. παρεδρεύω).†

title: προσεργάζομαι
content:
* προσ-εργάζομαι,

1. to work or do service besides (Hdt., Plut.).
2. to gain besides, by working or trading: Lk 19:16 (Xen.).†

title: προσέρχομαι
content:
προσ-έρχομαι, [in LXX for קרב, נגשׁ, etc.;]

to approach, draw near: absol., Mt 4:11, Lk 9:42, al.; c. infin., Mt 24:1, al.; c. dat. loc., He 12:18, 22; dat. pers., Mt 5:1, and freq., Jo 12:21, al.; ptcp., προσελθών, c. indic., Mt 8:2, and freq., Mk 1:31, Lk 7:14, al.; π. αὐτῷ, c. indic., Mt 4:3, Mk 6:35. Metaph.,
(a) of approaching God: absol. (Le 21:17, De 21:5, al.), He 10:1, 22; τ. θεῷ, He 7:25 11:6; τ. θρόνῳ τ. χάριτος, He 4:16; πρὸς Χριστόν, I Pe 2:4;
(b) in sense not found elsewhere (Field, Notes, 211), to consent to: ὑγιαίνουσι λόγοις, I Ti 6:3.

title: προσευχή
content:
† προσ-ευχή, -ῆς, ἡ (< προσεύχομαι), [in LXX chiefly for תְּפִלָּה;]

1. prayer to God: Mt 17:21 (WH, R, txt., om.) 21:22, Mk 9:29, Lk 22:45, Ac 3:1 6:4 10:31, Ro 12:12, I Co 7:5, Col 4:2; pl., Ac 2:42 10:4, Ro 1:10, Eph 1:16, Col 4:12, I Th 1:2, Phm 4, 22, I Pe 3:7 4:7, Re 5:8 8:3, 4; οἶκος προσευχῆς, Mt 21:13, Mk 11:17, Lk 19:46 (LXX); π. καὶ δέησις, Eph 6:18, Phl 4:6; pl., I Ti 2:1 5:5; ἡ π. τοῦ θεοῦ, prayer to God (cf. Wi 16:28), Lk 6:12; πρὸς τ. θεόν, seq. ὑπέρ, Ac 12:5; pl., Ro 15:30; Hebraistically (Bl., § 38, 3), προσευχῇ προσεύχεσθαι, Ja 5:17 (EV, prayed fervently).
2. a place of prayer: of a synagogue (III Mac 7:20, v.l.; v. Charles, APOT, i, 173; for other exx., v. Kennedy, Sources, 114); of a place in the open (FlJ, Ant., xiv, 10, 23), Ac 16:13, 16.†
SYN.: v.s. δέησις.

title: προσεύχομαι
content:
προσ-εύχομαι, [in LXX chiefly for פלל hith.;]

to pray (always of prayer to God, or in cl., to gods): absol., Mt 6:5–7, 9 14:23 19:13 26:36, 39, 41, 44, Mk 1:35 6:46 11:24, 25 13:33 (WH, R, txt., om.) Mk 14:32, 38, 39, Lk 1:10 3:21 5:16 6:12 9:18, 28, 29 11:1, 2 18:1, 10 22:44 (WH, R, mg., om.), Ac 1:24 6:6 9:11, 40 10:9, 30 11:5 12:12 13:3 14:23 16:25 20:36 21:5 22:17 28:8, I Co 11:4, 5 14:14, I Th 5:17, I Ti 2:8, Ja 5:13, 18; seq. λέγων, Mt 26:39, 42, Lk 22:41; c. dat. instr., I Co 11:5 14:14, 15; μακρά, Mt 23:14 (WH, R, txt., om.), Mk 12:40, Lk 20:47; ἐν πνεύματι (ἁγίῳ), Eph 6:18, Ju 20; προσευχῇ π. (a Hebraism, v.s. προσευχή), Ja 5:17; c. acc. rei, Lk 18:11, Ro 8:26; seq. ἐπί, c. acc. pers., Ja 5:14; c. dat. pers., Mt 6:6, I Co 11:13; seq. περί, c. gen., Ac 8:15, Col 1:3 4:3, I Th 5:25, II Th 1:11 3:1, He 13:18; ὑπέρ, Mt 5:44, Lk 6:28, Col 1:9, Ja 5:16; seq. ἵνα, Mt 24:20, Mk 13:18 14:35, Lk 22:46, I Co 14:13; τοῦτο ἵνα, Phl 1:9; c. inf., Lk 22:46; seq. τοῦ, c. inf. (Bl., § 71, 3), Ja 5:17.†

title: προσέχω
content:
προσ-έχω, [in LXX for קשׁב hi., שׁמר ni., etc.;]

1. to turn to, bring to (freq. ναῦν, expressed or understood, to bring to port, land; Hdt., al.).
2. τ. νοῦν, seq. dat., to turn one's mind to, attend to; in Xen. and later writers with νοῦν omitted (Bl., § 53, 1; 81, 1): Ac 8:6 16:14, He 2:1, II Pe 1:19; in sense of caring or providing for, Ac 20:28; π. ἑαυτῷ, to give heed to oneself (M, Pr., 157; cf. Ge 24:6, Ex 10:28, al.): Lk 17:3 21:34, Ac 5:35; id. seq. ἀπό (M, Pr., 102; Bl., § 34, 11; 40, 3; v.s. βλέπω), Lk 12:1; (without dat.) Mt 7:15 10:17 16:6, 11, 12, Lk 20:46 (cf. Si 6:13, al.); seq. μή, c. inf. (M, Pr., 193; Bl., § 69, 4), Mt 6:1.
3. to attach or devote oneself to: c. dat. pers., Ac 8:10, 11, I Ti 4:1; c. dat. rei, I Ti 1:4 3:8 4:13 6:3 T (-ερχ-, WH, R), Tit 1:14, He 7:13.†

title: προσηλόω
content:
** προσ-ηλόω, -ῶ, [in LXX: III Mac 4:9*;]

to nail to: c. acc. et dat., fig., Col 2:14.†

title: προσήλυτος
content:
† προσήλυτος, -ον (< προσελαύνω), [in LXX for גֵּר;]

1. one who has arrived, a stranger.
2. Of converts to Judaism, a proselyte (v. DB, s.v.): Mt 23:15, Ac 2:10 6:5 13:43.†

title: πρόσκαιρος
content:
** πρόσ-καιρος, -ον, [in LXX: IV Mac 15:2, 8, 23*;]

1. in season.
2. for a season, temporary, transient: II Co 4:18, He 11:25; of plants, short-lived: Mt 13:21, Mk 4:17.†

title: προσκαλέω
content:
προσ-καλέω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for קרא;]

to call to. Mid., to call to oneself (v. M, Pr., 157): c. acc. pers., Mt 10:1, Mk 3:13 6:7, Lk 7:19, Ac 5:40, Ja 5:14, al. Metaph., of the Divine call: Ac 2:39; c. inf., Ac 16:10 (v. Bl., § 69, 4); seq. εἰς, Ac 13:2.†

title: προσκαρτερέω
content:
προσ-καρτερέω, -ῶ (< καρτερός, strong, stedfast), [in LXX: Nu 13:21 (חזק hith.), To 5:8 א, Da Th Su 6*;]

to attend constantly, continue stedfastly, adhere to, wait on: c. dat. pers., Mk 3:9, Ac 8:13 10:7; c. dat. rei, Ac 1:14 2:42 6:4, Ro 12:12, Col 4:2; seq. ἐν, Ac 2:46; εἰς, Ro 13:6.†

title: προσκαρτέρησις
content:
*† προσ-καρτέρησις, -εως, ἡ (< προσκαρτερέω),

stedfastness, perseverance: Eph 6:18.†

title: προσκεφάλαιον
content:
προσ-κεφάλαιον, -ου, τό, [in LXX: Ez 13:18, 20 (כֶּסֶת), I Es 3:8*;]

a pillow, cushion: Mk 4:38.†

title: προσκληρόω
content:
*† προσ-κληρόω, -ῶ,

to allot to, assign to by lot; pass. (but perh. as mid., EV, consorted with, so Syr.): Ac 17:4 (for exx., v, Cremer, 749).†

title: πρόσκλησις
content:
πρόσ-κλησις, -εως, ἡ,

LTr., mg., for πρόσκλισις, q.v.

title: προσκλίνω
content:
** προσ-κλίνω, [in LXX: II Mac 14:24*;]

1. to make to lean against.
2. to make the scale incline one way or another; hence, metaph., of persons, to incline (sc. ἑαυτόν) towards: pass., Ac 5:36.†

title: πρόσκλισις
content:
*† πρόσ-κλισις, -εως, ἡ (< προσκλίνω),

inclination partiality: I Ti 5:21.†

title: προσκολλάω
content:
προσ-κολλάω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for דּבק;]

to glue to; pass., reflexive, to stick to, cleave to (Plat.): metaph. (c. dat., Jos 23:8, Si 6:34 al.), seq. πρός, Mk 10:7 (R, txt.), Eph 5:31(LXX).†

title: πρόσκομμα
content:
† πρόσ-κομμα, -τος, τό (< προσκόπτω), [in LXX: Ex 23:33 34:12 (מוֹקֵשׁ), Is 8:14 (נֶגֶף), Jth 8:22, Si 17:25, al.;]

(a) a stumble, stumbling: λίθος προσκόμματος (= אֶבֶן נֶגֶף, Is 8:14), fig., Ro 9:32, 33, I Pe 2:8(LXX);
(b) = προσκοπή, an occasion of stumbling, a stumbling-block: metaph., Ro 14:13, 20, I Co 8:9 (Plut.).†
SYN.: σκάνδαλον (cf. Cremer, 752 f.).

title: προσκοπή
content:
** προσκοπή, -ῆς, ἡ (< προσκόπτω), [in Gr. Ven.: Pr 16:18 (כִּשָּׁלוֹן)*;]

an occasion of stumbling, offence: II Co 6:3.†

title: προσκόπτω
content:
προσ-κόπτω, [in LXX for נגף, כּשׁל ni., etc.;]

1. trans., to strike (e.g. hand or foot) against: c. acc. seq. πρός, fig., Mt 4:6, Lk 4:11(LXX).
2. Intrans., to stumble: absol. (To 11:9, Pr 3:23), Jo 11:9, 10; of wind, to rush against, beat upon: c. dat, Mt 7:27. Metaph., in late writers,
(a) to offend (Polyb.);
(b) to take offence at, stumble at: seq. ἐν, Ro 14:21; c. dat., τ. λόγῳ, I Pe 2:8; τ. λίθῳ τ. προσκόμματος, Ro 9:32.†

title: προσκυλίω
content:
* προσ-κυλίω,

to roll up, roll to: c. acc. et dat., Mt 27:60; acc. seq. ἐπί, Mk 15:46.†

title: προσκυνέω
content:
προσ-κυνέω, -ῶ (< κυνέω, to kiss), [in LXX chiefly for שׁחה hith.;]

to make obeisance, do reverence to, worship;
(a) prop. (as in cl., of the gods: Hdt., Æsch., Plat., al.), of God, Christ and supra-mundane beings: absol., Jo 4:20 12:20, Ac 8:27 24:11, He 11:21 (Westc., in l.), Re 11:1; πίπτειν καὶ π., Re 5:14; c. dat. (of the significance of this constr. as compared with the usual cl., c. acc., v. Abbott, JG, 78 f.; JV, 133 ff.), Jo 4:21, 23, Ac 7:43, I Co 14:25, He 1:6, Re 4:10 7:11 11:16 13:4, 15 14:7 16:2 19:4, 10, 20 22:8, 9; c. acc. (v. supr.), Mt 4:10, Lk 4:8 24:52 (WH, R, mg., om.), Jo 4:22, 24, Re 9:20 13:4, 8, 12 14:9, 11 20:4; seq. ἐπώπιον, Lk 4:7, Re 15:4;
(b) as in cl., of homage to human superiors (cf. MM, xxi): absol., Mt 20:20, Ac 10:25; c. dat. (v. supr.), Mt 2:2, 8 8:2 9:18 14:33 15:25 18:26 28:9, Mk 15:19, Jo 9:38; πεσὼν π., Mt 2:11 4:9; ἐνώπιον τ. ποδῶν, Re 3:9; c. acc., Mk 5:6 (dat. T).†

title: προσκυνητήν
content:
*† προσ-κυνητής, -οῦ, ὁ (< προσκυνέω),

a worshipper: Jo 4:23.†

title: προσλαλέω
content:
προσ-λαλέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Ex 4:16 AB2 (דּבר pi.), Wi 13:17*;]

to speak to: Ac 28:20; c. dat. pers., Ac 13:43.†

title: προσλαμβάνω
content:
προσ-λαμβάνω, [in LXX: Ps 117 (18):16 (משׁה hi.), Ps 72 (73):24 (לקח), etc.;]

1. to take in addition.
2. to take to oneself, take, receive; in NT always mid., -ομαι;
(a) of things: of food, c. acc., Ac 27:33; c. gen. part., Ac 27:36;
(b) of persons: c. acc., Mt 16:22, Mk 8:32 (v. Swete, in l.), Ac 17:5 18:26 28:2, Ro 14:1, 3 15:7, Phm 17.†

title: πρόσλημψις
content:
* πρόσ-λημψις (Rec. -ληψις, as in Att.), -εως, ἡ (< προσλαμβάνω),

1. an assumption (Plat.).
2. a receiving (cf. προσλαμβάνω): Ro 11:15.†

title: προσμένω
content:
προσ-μένω, [in LXX: Jg 3:25 A (חוּל hi.), To 2:2 א, Wi 3:9, III Mac 7:17*;]

1. to wait longer, continue, remain still: Ac 18:18; seq. ἐν, I Ti 1:3.
2. C. dat., to remain with: Mt 15:32, Mk 8:32. Metaph., to remain attached to, cleave unto, abide in: τ. κυρίῳ, Ac 11:23 (R, txt.; ἐν τ. κ., R, mg., v. supr.); τ. χάριτι τ. θεοῦ, Ac 13:43; τ. δεήσεσιν, I Ti 5:5.†

title: προσορμίζω
content:
* προσ-ορμίζω (< ὅρμος, an anchorage),

to bring a ship to anchor at; usually in mid., to come to anchor near, and so pass. in late writers (Ael., Dio Cass.): Mk 6:53.†

title: προσοφείλω
content:
* προσ-οφείλω,

to owe besides: Phm 19 (v. Field, Notes, 225).†

title: προσοχθίζω
content:
† προσ-οχθίζω, [in LXX: Le 26:15, al. (גּעל); Le 18:25, al. (קוֹא), Ps 94 (95):10, Ez 36:31 (קוּט), Si 6:25, al. (other writers use ὀχθέω, rarely -ίζω);]

to be angry with: c. dat., He 3:10(LXX), 17.†

title: προσπαίω
content:
προσ-παίω = προσπίπτω,

Mt 7:25 L (v.s. προσπίπτω).†

title: πρόσπεινος
content:
*† πρόσπεινος, -ον (< πεῖωα, hunger),

hungry: Ac 10:10.†

title: προσπήγνυμι
content:
* προσ-πήγνυμι,

to fasten to: absol., to crucify, Ac 2:23.†

title: προσπίπτω
content:
προσ-πίπτω, [in LXX for נפל, נגע hi., כּרע;]

1. to fall upon, strike against: c. dat., of wind, Mt 7:25.
2. to fall down at one's feet, fall prostrate before: absol., seq. πρός, Mk 7:25; c. dat. pers., Mk 3:11 5:33, Lk 8:28, 47, Ac 16:29; τ. γόνασιν, Lk 5:8.†

title: προσποιέω
content:
προσ-ποιέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: I Ki 21:13 (14) (הלל hithpo.), Jb 19:14, Si 34 (31):30, Da LXX Su 11*;]

to make over to, add or attach to. Mid., to take to oneself, claim; hence, to pretend; c. inf. (cf. Xen., Anab., iv, 3, 20), to make as if: Lk 24:28.†

title: προσπορεύομαι
content:
προσ-πορεύομαι, [in LXX for קרב, נגשׁ, etc.;]

to come near, approach: c. dat. pers., Mk 10:35.†

title: προσρήγνυμι
content:
**† προσ-ρήγνυμι, [in Aq.: Ps 2:9*;]

to break against, dash against;
(a) trans. (παιδία πέτραις, FlJ, Ant., ix, 4, 6);
(b) intrans., c. dat.: Lk 6:48, 49 (cf. προσπίπτω).†

title: προστάσσω
content:
προσ-τάσσω, [in LXX chiefly for צוה pi.;]

1. c. acc. pers., to place at, to attach to.
2. to give a command, enjoin, appoint: Lk 5:14; c. dat. pers., Mt 1:24; c. acc. rei, Mt 8:4, Mk 1:44; c. acc. et inf., Ac 10:48; pass., Ac 10:33 17:26.†

title: προστάτις
content:
* προστάτις, -ιδος, ἡ (fem. of προστάτης),

a patroness, protectress: Ro 16:2.†

title: προστίθημι
content:
προσ-τίθημι, [in LXX chiefly for יסף hi., also for אסף ni., etc.;]

1. to put to.
2. to add, join to, give in addition: c. acc. seq. ἐπί, Mt 6:27, Lk 3:20 12:25; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, Ac 2:47; c. acc. et dat., Lk 17:5, He 12:19 (v. MM, xxi); pass., absol., Ac 2:41, Ga 3:19; c. dat., Mt 6:33, Mk 4:24, Lk 12:31, Ac 5:14 11:24; προσετέθη πρὸς τ. πατέρας (cf. Ge 26:8, Jg 2:10, al.), Ac 13:36; c. inf., of repeating or continuing the action signified by the following verb, as in Heb. idiom (Ge 4:2 8:12, al.; cf. WM, § 54, 5; Lft. on Clem., I Co., xii; but v. also M, Pr., 67, 233; Deiss., BS, 671; MM, xxi), Lk 20:11, Ac 12:3; similarly ptcp., προσθείς, c. indic. (Ge 38:5, al.), Lk 19:11.†

title: προστρέχω
content:
προσ-τρέχω, [in LXX for רוּץ;]

to run to: Mk 9:15 10:17, Ac 8:30.†

title: προσφάγιον
content:
*† προσφάγιον, -ου, τό (< φαγεῖν),

Hellenistic for ὄψον (v.s. ὀψάριον), a relish or dainty (esp. cooked fish), to be eaten with bread: Jo 21:5 (have ye taken any fish, Field, Notes, 109; Abbott, Essays, 105; cf. M, Pr., 170n; MM, Exp., xxi).†

title: πρόσφατος
content:
πρόσφατος, -ον (on the derivation, v. Boisacq, s.v. and cf. -ως), [in LXX: Nu 6:3 (לַח), De 32:17, Ec 1:9 (חָדָשׁ), Ps 80 (81):9 (זוּר), Si 9:10*;]

1. originally, freshly slain.
2. Generally (from Æsch. on), new, fresh, recent: ὁδός, He 10:20 (v. MM, Exp., xxi; Rutherford, NPhr., 471 f.).†

title: προσφάτως
content:
προσφάτως, adv. (v.s. πρόσφατος), [in LXX: De 24:5 (חָדָשׁ), Jth 4:3, 5, Ez 11:3, II Mac 14:36*;]

recently: Ac 18:2 (v. MM, Exp., xxi).†

title: προσφέρω
content:
προσ-φέρω, [in LXX chiefly for קרב hi.;]

1. to bring to, lead to: c. acc. et dat. pers., Mt 4:24 8:16 9:2, 32 14:35 17:16, Mk 2:4 (WH, R, txt.; sc. αὐτόν) 10:13, Lk 18:15 23:14; pass., Mt 12:22 (act., WH, txt.) 18:24 (προσήχθη, WH) 19:13; c. acc. rei, Mt 25:20; id. c. dat. pers., Mt 22:19, Lk 23:36; τ. στόματι, Jo 19:29; metaph., c. dat pers., to deal with, He 12:7 (cl.).
2. to offer: Mt 2:11, Ac 8:18; esp. (as freq. in LXX; cf. FlJ, Ant., iii, 9, 3) sacrifices, gifts and prayers to God: absol., seq. περί (ὑπέρ), Mk 1:44, Lk 5:14, He 5:1, 3 9:7 10:12; pass., Ac 21:26; c. acc. rei (δῶρον, θυσίαν, λυτρείαν, προσφοράν), Mt 5:23, 24 (aoristic pres.; M, Pr., 247) 8:4, Jo 16:2, Ac 7:42 21:26, He 5:1 8:3, 4 9:7, 9 10:1, 2, 8, 11, 12; δεήσεις τε κ. ἱκετηρίας, He 5:7; c. acc. pers., He 11:17 (conative impf.; M, Pr., 129); of Christ, He 7:27 (ἀνενέγκας, WH, txt.) 9:14, 25, 28.†

title: προσφιλής
content:
** προσφιλής, -ές (< φιλέω), [in LXX: Es 5:1, Si 4:7 20:13*;]

(a) of persons, in both act. and pass. sense (LXX, Es 5:1, Si 4:7 20:13);
(b) of things, pleasing, agreeable (EV, lovely): Phl 4:8.†

title: προσφορά
content:
προσ-φορά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< προσφέρω), [in LXX: III Ki 7:48 (פָּנִים) Ps 39 (40):6 (מִנְחָה), I Es 5:52, Si 14:11, al.;]

1. a bringing to, offering (Plat., al.).
2. (Less freq. in cl.), a present, an offering; in NT, of sacrificial offerings: Ac 21:26 24:17, Eph 5:2, He 10:5, 8, 14; περί ἁμαρτίας, He 10:18; c. gen. obj., Ro 15:16, He 10:10.†

title: προσφωνέω
content:
προσ-φωνέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: I Es 2:21 6:6, 22, II Mac 15:15*;]

1. to address, call to; in cl., c. acc. pers., c. dupl. acc. (cf. II Mac 15:15); absol. (Hom., Od., v, 159, al.): Ac 21:40. In late writers, c. dat. pers.: Mt 11:16, Lk 7:32 13:12 23:20, Ac 22:2.
2. to call by name, summon: c. acc. (as in cl.), Lk 6:13.†

title: πρόσχυσις
content:
*† πρόσ-χυσις, -εως, ἡ,

a pouring or sprinkling upon: He 11:28.†

title: προσψαύω
content:
* προσ-ψαύω,

in poët. and late writers, to touch: c. dat., Lk 11:46.†

title: προσωπολημπτέω
content:
*† προσωπολημπτέω (Rec. -ληπτ-), -ῶ (< -λήμπτης, q.v.),

to have respect of persons: Ja 2:9.†

title: προσωπολήμπτης
content:
*† προσωπο-λήμπτης (Rec. -λήπτης, v. Bl., § 6, 8), -ου, ὁ (< πρόσωπον λαμβάνειν, v.s. πρόσωπον),

a respecter of persons: Ac 10:34 (on this group of cognate forms, v. Mayor, ja., 78 f.; and cf. Thackeray, Gr., 44).†

title: προσωπολημψία
content:
*† προσωπολημψία (Rec. -ληψία), -ας, ἡ (< προσωπολήμπτης),

respect of persons: Ro 2:11, Eph 6:9, Col 3:25, Ja 2:1 (v. Mayor, in l.).†

title: πρόσωπον
content:
πρόσωπον, -ου, τό (< πρός, ὤψ), [in LXX chiefly and very freq. for פָּנִים;]

1. prop., of persons (so always in cl.);
(a) the face, countenance: Mt 6:16, 17, Mk 14:65, Lk 9:29, II Co 3:7, Re 4:7, al.; τὸ π. τῆς γενέσεως (EV, natural face), Ja 1:23; πίπτειν ἐπὶ (τὰ) π., Mt 17:6, Lk 5:12, Re 7:11, al.; ἀγνοούμενος τῷ π., Ga 1:22; π., οὐ καρδίᾳ, I Th 2:17; κατὰ πρόσωπον (in front, facing: Thuc., Xen., al.), when present, face to face, Ac 25:16, II Co 10:1, 7, Ga 2:11; id. c. gen., as compound prep., in the presence of (not cl.; v. Bl., § 40, 9; M, Pr., 99 f.; Thackeray, Gr., 43 f.), Lk 2:31, Ac 3:13; similarly ἀπὸ π. (Heb. מִלִּפְּנֵי; v. Dalman, Words, 29), from the presence of, Ac 3:19 5:41 7:45, II Th 1:9, Re 12:14 20:11; πρὸ π. (Heb. לִפְנֵי), before, Mt 11:10, Mk 1:2, Lk 7:27(LXX), al.; in other phrases resembling Heb. idiom (Thackeray, Gr., 42), βλέπειν (ὁρᾶν, θεωρεῖν, ἰδεῖν) τὸ π., to see one's face, i.e. see him in person, Mt 18:10, Ac 20:25, 38, I Th 3:10, Re 22:4; ἐμφανισθῆναι τῷ π. τοῦ θεοῦ, He 9:24; ἐν π. Χριστοῦ, II Co 2:10 4:6; μετὰ τοῦ π. σου, with thy presence, Ac 2:28(LXX); εἰς π. τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν, II Co 8:24; στηρίζειν τὸ π. (Heb. שׂוּם פָּנִים: Je 21:10, al.; v. Dalman, Words, 30), c. inf., to set one's face towards, Lk 9:51; similarly, τὸ π. αὐτοῦ ἦν πορευόμενον (op. cit., 31), Lk 9:53; τὸ π. τοῦ κυρίου ἐπί, I Pe 3:12(LXX);
(b) form, person: καυχᾶσθαι ἐν π. καὶ μὴ ἐν καρδίᾳ, II Co 5:12 (cf. I Ki 16:7); metaph., as in Heb. idiom, of judgment according to appearance, external condition or circumstances (נשָׂאָ פָּנִים; v. Dalman, Words, 30; Thackeray, Gr., 43 f.): λαμβάνειν π., Lk 20:21, Ga 2:6; βλέπειν εἰς π., Mt 22:16, Mk 12:14; θαυμάζειν πρόσωπα, Ju 16.
2. Of things (cf. Dalman, Words, 30);
(a) face, appearance (Ps 103 (104):30): Mt 16:3 (WH, R, mg., om.), Lk 12:56, Ja 1:11;
(b) surface (Ge 2:6): Lk 21:35, Ac 17:26.

title: προτάσσω
content:
** προ-τάσσω, [in LXX: II Mac 8:36 R (Α, προστ-)*;]

1. to place in front.
2. to arrange beforehand: Ac 17:26, Rec. (for προστ., Edd.).†

title: προτείνω
content:
** προ-τείνω, [in LXX: II Mac7, III Mac 2:1*;]

to stretch out, stretch forth: of preparations for scourging (v. Field, Notes, 136 f.), Ac 22:25.†

title: πρότερος
content:
πρότερος, and πρῶτος, compar. and superl. from πρό, opp. to ὕστερος, ὕστατος.

A. Compar., πρότερος, -α, -ον, [in LXX for לִפָנִים, רִאשׁוֹן, etc.;]

before, of time, place, rank, etc.; in NT always of Time, before, former: Eph 4:22. Adverbially, πρότερον, before, aforetime, formerly: Jo 7:50, II Co 1:15, He 4:6; opp. to ἔπειτα, He 7:27; τὸ π., Jo 6:62 9:8, Ga 4:13, I Ti 1:13; αἱ π. ἡμέραι, He 10:32; αἱ π. ἐπιθυμίαι, I Pe 1:14.†

title: πρῶτος
content:
πρότερος, and πρῶτος, compar. and superl. from πρό, opp. to ὕστερος, ὕστατος.

B. Superl., πρῶτος, -η, -ον, [in LXX chiefly for רִאשׁוֹן, also for אֶחַד, etc.;]

first,
1. of Time or Place;
(a) absol., as subst., ὁ π.., Lk 14:18, Jo 19:32, I Co 14:30; ὁ π. καὶ ὁ ἔσχατος, Re 1:17 2:8 22:13; neut., τὸ π., opp. to τ. δεύτερον, He 10:9; τὰ π., opp. to τ. ἔσχατα, Mt 12:45, Lk 11:26, II Pe 2:20; anarth., Mt 10:2; pl., Mt 19:30, Mk 10:31, Lk 13:30; ἐν πρώτοις (EV, first of all), I Co 15:3;
(b) as adj.: πρώτῃ (sc. ἡμέρᾳ) σαββάτου, Mk 16:[9]; φυλακή, opp. to δευτέρα, Ac 12:10; equiv. to adv. in English, Jo 8:[7] 20:4, 8, Ac 27:43, Ro 10:19, I Ti 1:16, I Jo 4:19; = πρότερος (v. infr.; cf. M, Pr., 79; Bl., § 11, 5; Thackeray, Gr., 183 f.): c. gen., π. μου ἦν (my chief: Abbott, Jg., 509 ff.; but cf. M, Pr., 245), Jo 1:15, 30; c. art., Mk 14:12, Ac 1:1, al.; seq. ὁ δεύτερος, etc., Mt 22:25, Mk 12:20, al.
2. Of Rank or Dignity, chief, principal: Mt 20:27 22:38, Mk 9:35, Eph 6:2, al.; c. gen., Mk 12:28, 29 al.; πόλις (Field, Notes, 124), Ac 16:12; c. art., Lk 15:22 19:47, Ac 13:50, al.
3. Neut., πρῶτον, as adv., first, at the first;
(a) of Time: Mt 8:21, Mk 4:28, al.; τὸ π., Jo 10:40, al.;
(b) of Order: Ro 3:2, I Co 11:18, al.

title: προτίθημι
content:
προ-τίθημι, [in LXX: Ex 40:4, 23, Le 24:8 (ערךְ) Ps 53 (54):3 (שׂוּם), etc.;]

1. to set before, set forth publicly; so also in mid.: c. acc. pers., Ro 3:25 (for a suggested alt. rend., v. MM, xxii).
2. Mid., to set before oneself, propose, purpose: c. inf., Ro 1:13; c. acc. rei, Eph 1:9.†

title: προτρέπω
content:
** προ-τρέπω, [in LXX: Wi 14:18, II Mac 11:7, IV Mac 12:7 15:12 16:13*;]

to urge forwards, exhort, persuade. Mid., in same sense (as also in cl.): Ac 18:27.†

title: προτρέχω
content:
προ-τρέχω, [in LXX: I Ki 8:11 (לִפְנֵי רוּץ), Jb 41:13 (14) A (דּוּץ), To 11:3 (seq. ἔμπροσθεν), I Mac 16:21*;]

1. to run forward.
2. to run on, run in advance: Jo 20:4; seq. εἰς τὸ ἔμπροσθεν, Lk 19:4.†

title: προϋπάρχω
content:
** προ-ϋπ-άρχω, [in LXX: Jb 42:18*;]

1. to be beforehand in.
2. to be before or previously: c. ptcp., Lk 23:12, Ac 8:9.†

title: πρόφασις
content:
πρό-φασις, -εως, ἡ (< φήμι), [in LXX: Ps 140 (141):4 (עֲלִילָה), Da TH 6:4, 5 (5, 6) (עִלָּה), Pr 18:1, Ho 10:4*;]

a pretence, pretext: Mt 23:1 (WM, R, txt., om.), Mk 12:40, Lk 20:47, Jo 15:22, Ac 27:30, Phl 1:18, I Th 2:5.†

title: προφέρω
content:
προ-φέρω, [in LXX: Pr 10:13 (מצא ni.), To 9:5, al.;]

to bring forth: c. acc. rei, seq. ἐκ, Lk 6:45.†

title: προφητεία
content:
† προφητεία, -ας, ἡ (< προψητεύω), [in LXX for נְבוּאָה, חָזוֹן;]

the gift (and its exercise) of interpreting the Divine will and purpose, prophecy, prophesying: of OT prophecy, Mt 13:14, II Pe 1:20, 21; of NT prophecy, Ro 12:6, I Co 12:10 13:2 14:6, 22, I Ti 4:14, Re 11:6 22:19; pl., I Co 13:8, I Th 5:20, I Ti 1:18; οἱ λόγοι τῆς π., Re 1:3 22:7, 10, 18; τ. πνεῦμα τῆς π., Re 19:10 (Luc., FlJ, LXX, π.; v. Deiss., BS, 235 f.; MM, xxii).†

title: προφητεύω
content:
προφητεύω (< προφήτης), [in LXX chiefly for נבא ni., hith.;]

to be a προφήτης (q.v.), to prophesy: in the primary sense of telling forth the Divine counsels, Mt 7:22 26:68, Mk 14:65, Lk 1:67 22:64, Ac 19:6, I Co 11:4, 5 13:9 14:1, 3–5, 24, 31, 39, Re 11:3; with the idea of foretelling future events (an idea merely incidental, not essential; v. Lft., Notes, 83 f.), Mt 11:13, Ac 2:17, 18(LXX) 21:9; seq. περί, Mt 15:7, Mk 7:6, I Pe 1:10; ἐπί, c. dat., Re 10:11; λέγων, Ju 14; ὅτι, Jo 11:51.†
SYN.: μαντεύομαι, q.v.

title: προφήτης
content:
προφήτης, -ου, ὁ [< πρόφημι, to speak forth), [in LXX chiefly for נָבִיא;]

one who acts as an interpreter or forth-teller of the Divine will (v. Lft., Notes, 83 f.; Tr., Syn., § vi), a prophet;
1. in cl. (Æsch., Hdt., Plat., al.), of the interpreters of oracles.
2. In NT,
(a) of the OT prophets: Mt 5:12, Mk 6:15, Lk 4:27, Jo 8:52, Ro 11:3, al.;
(b) of prophets in general: Mt 10:41 13:57 21:46, Mk 6:4, Lk 13:33, al.;
(c) of John the Baptist: Mt 21:26, Mk 6:15, Lk 1:76;
(d) of Christ: Mt 21:11, Jo 6:14, Ac 3:22, 23 7:37 (LXX);
(e) of Christian prophets in the apostolic age: Ac 15:32, I Co 12:28, Eph 2:20, al.;
(f) by meton., of the writings of prophets: Lk 24:27, Ac 8:28, al.;
(g) of a poet: Tit 1:12 (on the use of the term in π. and Inscr., v. Deiss., BS, 235 f.; MM, xxii).

title: προφητικός
content:
*† προφητικός, -ά, -όν (< προφήτης),

of prophecy, prophetic: Ro 16:26, II Pe 1:19.†

title: προφῆτις
content:
προφῆτις, -ιδος, ἡ fem, of προφήτης, [in LXX: Ex 15:20, Jg 4:4, IV Ki 22:14, II Ch 34:22, Is 8:3 (נְבִיאָה)*;]

a prophetess: Lk 2:36, Re 2:20.†

title: προφθάνω
content:
προ-φθάνω, [in LXX chiefly for קדם pi.;]

c. ptcp. (as in cl., but more freq. the simple φθάνω, q.v.), to anticipate: Mt 17:25.†

title: προχειρίζω
content:
προ-χειρίζω (< πρόχειρος, at hand), [in LXX: Ex 4:13 (שׁלח), Jos 3:12 (לקח), Da LXX 3:22, II Mac 3:7 8:9 14:12 A*;]

1. to put into the hand, deliver up: pass., Ac 3:20.
2. More freq. as depon., -ομαι, to take into one's hand; hence, metaph., to propose, determine, choose: c. inf., Ac 22:14; c. acc. pers., Ac 26:16.†

title: προχειροτονέω
content:
* προ-χειρο-τονέω, -ῶ (v. χειροτονέω),

to choose or appoint beforehand: Ac 10:41 (Plat., al.).†

title: Πρόχορος
content:
Πρόχορος, -ου, ὁ,

Prochorus: Ac 6:5.

title: πρύμνα
content:
* πρύμνα, -ης, ἡ,

prop. fem. of adj. πρύμνος, -η, -ον, (sc. ναῦς), the hindmost part of a ship, the stern: Mk 4:38, Ac 27:29; opp. to πρῷρα, Ac 27:41.†

title: πρωί
content:
πρωί (Rec. πρωΐ), adv. (< πρό), [in LXX chiefly for בֹּקֶר, בַּבֹּקֶר;]

in the morning, early: Mt 16:3 (R, txt.) 21:18, Mk 1:35 11:20 13:35 15:1 16:[9], Jo 18:28 20:1; λίαν π., Mk 16:2; ἅμα π., Mt 20:1; ἀπὸ π. (cf. ἀπὸ πρωΐθεν, Ex 18:13), Ac 28:23.†

title: πρωία
content: πρωία, v.s. πρώιος.

title: πρώϊμος
content: πρώϊμος, v.s. πρόϊμος.

title: πρωινός
content:
† πρωινός (Rec. -ϊνος, v. WH, App., ή, -όν (< πρωί), [in LXX chiefly for בֹּקֶר;] = cl. πρώιος,

at early morn, early: ἀστήρ, Re 2:28 22:16.†

title: πρώιος
content:
πρώιος (Rec. -ϊος), -α, -ον (< πρωί), [in LXX for בֹּקֶר, לַּ׳, בַּ׳;]

at early morn, early; as subst., ἡ π. (sc. ὥρα, cf. ἡ ὥ. ἡ π., III Mac 5:24), early morning: Mt 27:1, Jo 21:4.†

title: πρῷρα
content:
* πρῷρα (Rec. incorrectly πρώρα, v. Bl., § 3, 3; LS, s.v.), -ης (for Att. -ας, v. Bl., § 7, 1; Mayser, l 2), ἡ,

the forward part of a ship, the prow: Ac 27:30; opp. to πρύμνα, Ac 27:41.†

title: πρωτεύω
content:
πρωτεύω (< πρῶτος), [in LXX: Es 5:11, II Mac 6:18 13:15*;]

to be first, pre-eminent, have the first place: Col 1:18.†

title: πρωτοκαθεδρία
content:
*† πρωτοκαθεδρία, -ας, ἡ (< πρῶιος, καθέδρα),

the chief seat: Mt 23:6, Mk 12:39 (v. Swete, in l.), Lk 11:43 20:46.†

title: πρωτοκλυτία
content:
*† πρωτο-κλισία, -ας, ἡ,

the chief place at table (v. Swete, Mk 12:39): Mt 23:6, Mk 12:39, Lk 14:7, 8 20:46.†

title: πρῶτον
content: πρῶτον, πρῶτος, v.s. πρότερος.

title: πρωτοστάτης
content:
πρωτοστάτης, -ου, ὁ (< πρῶτος, ἵστημι), [in LXX: Jb 15:24 AB*;]

prop., of soldiers, one who stands first, one in the front rank (Thuc., Xen.); hence, metaph., a leader: Ac 24:5.†

title: πρωτοτόκια
content:
† πρωτοτόκια, -ων, τά (< πρωτότοκος), [in LXX (with v.l. -εῖα, -εία): Ge 25:31 ff. 27:36, De 21:17, I Ch 5:1 (בְּכוֹרָה)*;]

the rights of the first-born, birthright (= cl. ἡ πρεσβεία): He 12:16.†

title: πρωτότοκος
content:
πρωτότοκος, -ον (< πρῶτος, τίκτω), [in LXX chiefly for בְּכוֹר;]

first-born: Lk 2:7; pl., He 11:28. Metaph., of the priority of Christ (originally perh. a Messianic title, cf. Ps 88 (89):28, He 1:6; v. ICC on Col 1:15): He 1:6; π. πάσης κτίσεως, Col 1:15; ἐν πολλοῖς ἀδελφοῖς, Ro 8:29; π. (ἐκ) τ. νεκρῶν, Col 1:18, Re 1:5; pl., of the elect, ἐκκλησία πρωτοτόκων, He 12:23.†

title: πρώτως
content:
* πρώτως, adv.,

first: Ac 11:26.†

title: πταίω
content:
πταίω, [in LXX chiefly for נגף ni.;]

1. trans., to cause to stumble (I Ki 4:3, cf. Deiss., BS, 681).
2. Intrans., to stumble. Metaph., in moral sense, Ro 11:11, Ja 2:10 3:2, II Pe 1:10.†

title: πτέρνα
content:
πτέρνα, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX for עָקֵב;]

the heel: fig., ἐπαίρειν τὴν π. ἐπί, Jo 13:18(LXX).†

title: πτερύγιον
content:
πτερύγιον, -ου, -τό (dimin. of πτέρυξ), [in LXX chiefly for כָּנָף;]

1. a little wing.
2. Anything like a wing, as a turret, battlement: τ. ἱεροῦ, Mt 4:5, Lk 4:9.†

title: πτέρυξ
content:
πτέρυξ, -υγος, ἡ (< πέτομαι), [in LXX chiefly for כָּנָף;]

a wing: of birds, Mt 23:37, Lk 13:34, Re 12:14; of creatures seen in a vision, Re 4:8 9:9.†

title: πτηνός
content:
** πτηνός, -ή, -όν (< πέτομαι), [in Aq.: Jb 5:7*;]

winged; as subst., τὰ π., birds: I Co 15:39.†

title: πτοέω
content:
πτοέω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for חתת ni.;]

to terrify. Pass., to be terrified: Lk 21:9 24:37 (WH, mg., θροηθέντες).†

title: πτόησις
content:
πτόησις, -εως, ἡ (< πτοέω), [in LXX: Pr 3:25 (פַּחַד), Sir 50:4 א1, I Mac 3:25 R*;]

a fluttering, excitement, caused by any emotion, but esp. by fear, hence, terror: φοβεῖσθαι πτόησιν, to be afraid with (cogn. acc.) or of any terror (v. ICC, in l.): I Pe 3:6.†

title: Πτολεμαΐς
content:
Πτολεμαΐς, -ΐδος, ἡ,

Ptolemais, a maritime city of Phœnicea: Ac 21:7.†

title: πτύον
content:
** πτύον, -ου, τό, [in Sm.: Is 30:24*;]

a winnowing shovel or fan: Mt 3:12, Lk 3:17.†

title: πτύρομαι
content:
* πτύρομαι, depon.,

to be startled, frightened: Phl 1:28. (The active πτύρω is also found in some late writers.)†

title: πτύσμα
content:
* πτύσμα, -τος, τό, (< πτύω),

spittle: Jo 9:6 (Hipp., Polyb., al.).†

title: πτύσσω
content:
* πτύσσω,

to fold; of a scroll, to roll up: βιβλίον, Lk 4:20 (cf. ἀνα-πτύσσω).†

title: πτύω
content:
πτύω, [in LXX: Nu 12:14 (ירק), Si 28:12*;]

to spit: Mk 7:33 8:23, Jo 9:6 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐμ-πτύω).†

title: πτῶμα
content:
πτῶμα, -τος, τό (< πίπτω), [in LXX: Jg 14:8 (מַפֶּלֶת), Jb 16:15 (14) (פֶּרֶץ), Is 51:19 (שֹׁד), Jth 8:19, Wi 4:18, al.;]

1. a fall, metaph., a misfortune, calamity (Trag., Plat., Polyb., al.; LXX).
2. That which has fallen;
(a) of buildings, a ruin (Polyb.);
(b) of living creatures, in cl. (poët. only) usually c. gen., νεκρῶν, etc., but also absol., as in late writers and NT, a fallen body, a carcase, corpse: Mt 14:12 24:28, Mk 15:45; π. αὐτοῦ, Mk 6:29; αὐτῶν, Re 11:8, 9 (cf. Rutherford, NPhr., 472 f.).†

title: πτῶσις
content:
πτῶσις, -εως, ἡ (< πίπτω), [in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶף, מַפֶּלֶת, and cogn. forms;]

a falling, fall (Plat., Plut., al.): Mt 7:27; metaph., Lk 2:34.†

title: πτωχεία
content:
πτωχεία, -ας, ἡ (< πτωχεύω), [in LXX chiefly for עֳנִי;]

beggary, destitution: II Co 8:2, 9, Re 2:9.†

title: πτωχεύω
content:
πτωχεύω (< πτωχός), [in LXX: Jg 6:6, Ps 78 (79):8 (דּלל); Jg 14:15 A, Pr 23:21 (ירשׁ); Ps 33 (34):10 (רוּשׁ), To 4:21*;]

1. to be a beggar, to beg (so chiefly in cl.).
2. to be poor as a beggar, to be destitute, poor: opp. to πλούσιος ὤν, II Co 8:9.†

title: πτωχός
content:
πτωχός, -ή, -όν (< πτώσσω, to crouch, cower), [in LXX for עָנִי, דַּל, רָשׁ, etc.;]

of one who crouches and cowers, hence,
1. as subst., a beggar: Lk 14:13, 21 16:20, 22.
2. As adj.,
(a) prop., beggarly: metaph., στοιχεῖα, Ga 4:9 (v. Lft., in l.);
(b) in broader sense (opp. to πλούσιος), poor: Mt 11:5 19:21 26:9, 11, Mk 10:21 12:42, 43 14:5, 7, Lk 4:18 7:22 18:22 19:8 21:3, Jo 12:5, 6, 8 13:29, Ro 15:26, II Co 6:10, Ga 2:10, Ja 2:2, 3, 6, Re 13:16; π. τ. κόσμῳ, Ja 2:5; metaph., Lk 6:20, Re 3:17; π. τ. πνεύματι, Mt 5:3.†
SYN.: πένης, q.v.

title: πυγμή
content:
πυγμή, -ῆς, ἡ, [in LXX: Ex 21:18, Is 58:4 (אֶגְרוֹף)*;]

the fist: πυγμῇ νίψασθαι τ. χεῖρας (T, πυκνά; Vg., Goth., Copt., crebro), to wash the hands with the fist (diligently, R, txt.; up to the elbow, R, mg.; the exact meaning is doubtful; v. Swete, in l.): Mk 7:3.†

title: πύθων
content:
* πύθων, -ωνος, ὁ,

1. in cl., Python, a serpent slain by Apollo, who is hence surnamed the Pythian.
2. In Plut. (ii, 414 E), a name given to ventriloquist soothsayers (ἐγγαστρίμυθοι; cf. Le 19:31 20:6, 27, I Ki 28:7), and perhaps in this sense πνεῦμα πύθωνα, a python-spirit: Ac 16:16.†

title: πυκιός
content:
πυκιός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX: Ez 31:3 A (חֹרֶשׁ), III Mac 1:28 4:10, IV Mac 12:12*;]

1. close, compact, solid.
2. frequent: I Ti 5:23. Neut. pl., πυκνά, as adv., much, often: Mk 7:3 T (v.s. πυγμή), Lk 5:33. Comparat., πυκνότερον, very often or so much the oftener (v. Bl., § 44, 3n): Ac 24:26.†

title: πυκτεύω
content:
* πυκτεύω (< πύκτης, a pugilist),

to box: I Co 9:26.†

title: πύλη
content:
πύλη, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly and very freq. for שַׁעַר sometimes for דֶּלֶת, פֶּתַח;]

a gate: Lk 7:12, Ac 9:24 12:10 16:13, He 13:12; ἡ Ὡραία Π. τ. ἱεροῦ, Ac 3:10. Metaph., Mt 7:13, 14; πύλαι ᾅδου (Wi 16:13, III Mac 5:51, and cf. κλεῖς ᾅδου, Re 1:18): Mt 16:18.†

title: πυλών
content:
πυλών, -ῶνος, ὁ (< πύλη), [in LXX chiefly for פֶּתַח, שַׁעַר;]

1. the porch or vestibule of a house or palace: Mt 26:71, Lk 16:20, Ac 10:17 12:13, 14.
2. The gate-way or gate-tower of a walled town: Ac 14:13, Re 21:12, 13, 15, 21, 25 22:14.†

title: πυνθάνομαι
content:
πυνθάνομαι, [in LXX for דּרשׁ;]

1. to inquire: c. acc. rei, Jo 4:42, Ac 23:20; seq. quæst. indir., Mt 2:4, Lk 15:26 18:36, Ac 10:18 21:33; quæst. dir., Ac 4:7 10:29 23:19; seq. παρά, c. gen. pers., Mt 2:4, Jo 4:52.
2. to learn by inquiry: seq. ὅτι, Ac 23:34.†

title: πῦρ
content:
πῦρ, gen., πυρός, τό, [in LXX chiefly and very freq. for אֵשׁ;]

fire: Mk 9:22, Lk 3:9, Jo 15:6, Ac 2:19, I Co 3:13, Ja 3:5, Re 8:5, al; π. καὶ θεῖον, Lk 17:29; κατακαίειν (ἐν) π., Mt 13:40, Re 17:16 18:8; καίεσθαι πυρί, He 12:18, Re 8:8 21:8; φλὸξ πυρός, Ac 7:30, II Th 1:8, He 1:7, Re 1:14 2:18 19:12; λαμπάδες πυρός, Re 4:5; στῦλοι πυρός, Re 10:1; ἄνθρακες πυρός, Ro 12:20(LXX); γλῶσσαι ὡσεὶ πυρός, Ac 2:3; δοκιμάζειν (πυροῦσθαι) διὰ πυρός, I Pe 1:7, Re 3:18; ὡς διὰ. π. (Lft., Notes, 193), I Co 3:15. Of the fire of hell (cf. Dalman, Words,161): Mk 9:48(LXX); τὸ π. τὸ αἰώνιον, Mt 18:8 25:41 (cf. IV Mac 12:12); ἄσβεστον, Mk 9:43; πυρὸς αἰωνίου δίκην ὑπέχειν, Ju 7; γέεννα τοῦ π., Mt 5:22 18:9; κάμινος τοῦ π., Mt 13:42, 50; ἡ λίμνη τοῦ π., Re 19:20 20:10, 14, 15; πυρὶ τηρεῖσθαι, II Pe 3:7; βασανισθῆναι ἐν π., Re 14:10. Metaph.: βαπτίζειν πυρί, Mt 3:11, Lk 3:16; of the tongue, Ja 3:5; of strife and discord, Lk 12:49; ἐκ π. ἁρπάζειν, Ju 23; πυρὶ ἁλίζεσθαι, Mk 9:49; ζῆλος πυρός, He 10:27; of God, π. καταναλίσκον, He 12:29(LXX).

title: πυρά
content:
** πυρά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< πῦρ), [in LXX: Jth 7:5, Wi 17:6, al.;]

a fire: Ac 28:2, 3.†

title: πύργος
content:
πύργος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for מִגְדָּל;]

a tower: Lk 13:4; of a watch-tower in a vineyard (Is 5:2): Mt 21:33, Mk 12:1, and prob., Lk 14:28.†

title: πυρέσσω
content:
* πυρέσσω (< πῦρ),

to be ill of a fever: Mt 8:14, Mk 1:3.†

title: πυρετός
content:
πυρετός, -οῦ, ὁ (< πῦρ), [in LXX: De 28:22 (קדַּחַת)*;]

a fever: Mt 8:15, Mk 1:31, Lk 4:39, Jo 4:52, Ac 28:8; π. μέγας, a high fever: Lk 4:38 (on the technical phrase here, v. MM, xxii).†

title: πύρινος
content:
πύρινος, -η, -ον, [in LXX: Ez 28:14, 16 (אֵשׁ), Si 48:9*;]

fiery: Re 9:17.†

title: πυρόω
content:
πυρόω, -ῶ (< πῦρ), [in LXX chiefly for צרף;]

to set on fire, burn up. In NT always pass.,
1. to be set on fire, to burn: Eph 6:16, II Pe 3:12; ptcp., glowing, Re 1:15. Metaph., of grief or indignation, II Co 11:29; of lust, I Co 7:9.
2. Of metals (cf. Jb 22:25, Ps 11 (12):7, Za 13:9), to be refined or purified by fire: Re 3:18 (and so in RV, Re 1:15, but v. supr.).†

title: πυρράζω
content:
† πυρράζω (< πυρρός), [in LXX, πυρρίζω: Le 13:19, 42 ff. 14:37 (אֲדַמְדָּם)*;]

to be fiery red: Mt 16:|[2, 3]|.†

title: πυρρός
content:
πυρρός, -ά, -όν (< πῦρ), [in LXX for אֱדֹם;]

fiery red: Re 6:4 12:3.†

title: Πυρρός
content:
Πύρρος, -ου, ὁ,

Pyrrhus: Ac 20:4.†

title: πύρωσις
content:
πύρωσις, -εως, ἡ (< πυρόω), [in LXX: Pr 27:21 (כּוּר), Am 4:9 (שִׁדָּפוֹן)*;]

1. a burning: Re 18:9, 18.
2. a refining or trial by fire: metaph., I Pe 4:12.†

title: πω
content:
πω, enclit. part.,

yet, v.s. μή-πω, μηδέ-πω, οὔ-πω, οὐδέ-πω, πώ-ποτε.

title: πωλέω
content:
πωλέω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for מכר;]

1. to exchange or barter.
2. to sell: Lk 17:28, Re 13:17; οἱ πωλοῦντες, Mt 21:12 25:9, Mk 11:15, Lk 19:45; c. acc. rei, Mt 13:44 19:21 21:12, Mk 10:21 11:15, Lk 12:33 18:22 22:36, Jo 2:14, 16, Ac 5:1 (sc. αὐτά, αὐτόν), Ac 4:34, 37. Pass., I Co 10:25; c. gen. pretii, Mt 10:29, Lk 12:6.†

title: πῶλος
content:
πῶλος, -ου, ὁ (in cl. also ἡ), [in LXX chiefly for עַיִר;]

a foal, colt, prop., of a horse, then the young of other animals; in NT of the colt of an ass: Mt 21:2, 5(LXX), 7, Mk 11:2, 4, 5, 7, Lk 19:30, 33, 35, Jo 12:15(LXX).†

title: πώποτε
content:
πώ-ποτε, adv.,

ever yet: Lk 19:30, Jo 1:18 5:37 6:35 8:33, I Jo 4:12.†

title: πωρόω
content:
πωρόω, -ῶ (< πῶρος, 1. a stone. 2. a callus), [in LXX: Jb 17:7 B (כּהה), Pr 10:20 A*;]

to petrify, harden, form a callus. Metaph., π. τ. καρδίαν, Jo 12:40. Pass., Ro 11:7; τ. νοήματα, II Co 3:14; ἡ καρδία, Mk 6:52 8:17.†

title: πώρωσις
content:
* πώρωσις, -εως, ἡ (< πωρόω),

a covering with a callus, a hardening: metaph., Mk 3:6, Ro 11:25, Eph 4:18.†

title: πως
content:
πως, enclit. part.,

at all; v.s. εἴπως, μήπως.

title: πῶς
content:
πῶς, interrog. adv., correl. of ὅπως,

1. prop., in direct questions, how?: c. indic., Mt 12:29, Mk 3:23, Lk 11:18, Jo 3:4, al.; καὶ π., Mk 4:13, Lk 20:44; π. οὖν, Mt 12:26; π. οὐ, Mt 16:11, Lk 12:56; in deliberative questions (cf. Bl., § 64, 6), c. subjc., Mt 23:33 26:54; π. οὖν, Ro 10:14; π. δέ, Ro 10:14, 15; seq. ἄν, c. optat., Ac 8:31.
2. As sometimes in cl. but more freq. and increasingly so in late writers (v. WM, § 57, 2; Bl., § 70, 2; Thumb, MGr., 192; Jannaris, Gr., App., vi, 13 f.), = ὅπως, ὥς;
(a) in indirect discourse: c. indic., Mt 6:28, Mk 12:41, Lk 8:36, Jo 9:15, Ac 9:27, al.; c. subjc., Mk 11:18, Lk 12:11;
(b) in exclamations: Mt 21:20, Mk 10:23, 24, Lk 12:50 18:24, Jo 11:36.
